paper.title: Fighting Bandits with a New Kind of Smoothness

unmapped: Loss vectors lie in [-1,0]^N (range of width 1, non-positive 'loss-only' assumption) rather than [0,1]; the analysis critically uses non-positivity
settings.definition_quote: On each round $t = 1,\ldots, T$, a learner must choose a distribution $p_t \in \D_N$ over the set of $N$ available actions. The adversary (Nature) chooses a loss vector $\xx_t \in [-1,0]^N$. The learner plays action $i_t$ sampled according to $p_t$ and suffers the loss $\xx_{t,{i_t}}$. The learner observes only a single coordinate

algorithms.name: GBPA with stochastic smoothing / FTPL with Geometric Resampling

source.label: thm:tsallis
source.quote: Let $\tf(\XX) = \max_{p \in \D_N}\{\langle p, \XX \rangle - \eta S_\alpha(p) \}$. Then the GBPA$(\tf)$ has regret at most \EE\Regret \leq \eta \frac{N^{1 - \alpha} - 1}{1-\alpha} + \frac{N^\alpha T}{2 \eta \alpha}.

results.notes: N = K. Bound holds for any fixed eta (no tuning to T), so marked anytime; tuned version in corollary requires T.

bound.regime: alpha in (0,1), eta = sqrt(T(1-alpha)/(2 alpha)) N^{alpha-1/2}

source.quote: For any $\alpha \in (0,1)$, if we choose $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{T(1-\alpha)}{2\alpha}} N^{\alpha-\frac{1}{2}}$ then we have \EE\Regret \leq \sqrt{\frac{2 T N}{\alpha(1-\alpha) }}.

results.notes: Tuning of eta depends on T.

source.quote: In particular, the choice of $\alpha = \frac 1 2$ gives a regret of no more than $2\sqrt{2 T N}$, recovering \citep[Theorem~5.7]{bubeck2012regret}.

results.notes: Same bound as INF in Bubeck & Cesa-Bianchi; paper notes it recovers it.

bound.regime: D continuous, unbounded towards +infinity, bounded hazard rate

symbols.EmaxZ: expected maximum of K iid draws from perturbation distribution D
symbols.h_sup: supremum of the hazard rate f/(1-F) of D

extra_assumptions: perturbation distribution has bounded hazard rate

source.quote: The regret of the GBPA with $\tf(\XX) = \EE_{Z_1, \ldots, Z_n \sim D} \max_{i} \{\XX_{i} +  \eta Z_{i}\}$ is at most: \eta \EE[\max_{i} Z_{i}] + \frac{N(\sup h_\mathcal{D})}{\eta}T

results.notes: For exact GBPA (expectation-gradient), not the sampled FTPL; numbering inferred from section-based counter.

bound.regime: distributions of Table 1 with stated parameters; M = sqrt(NT) Geometric Resampling iterations

extra_assumptions: perturbation distribution from Table 1 (Gumbel, Frechet, Weibull, Pareto, Gamma) with restricted parameters

source.quote: Follow the Perturbed Leader Algorithm with distributions in Table \ref{tab:distributions} (restricted to a certain range of parameters),  combined with Geometric Resampling (Section \ref{sec:ftpl:ftpl}) with $M = \sqrt{NT}$,	 has an expected regret of order $O(\sqrt{TN \log N})$.

results.notes: Text elsewhere says M = NT suffices; the GR bias term NT/(eM) with M=sqrt(NT) gives sqrt(NT)/e, consistent. Eta tuning requires T.
